correctness.rationale: A distance-two selected pair obstructs the other diagonal of the square. Conversely, at each geodesic step with at least two remaining flips, the distance-decreasing neighbors are pairwise at distance two and cannot all be selected. Maximality is therefore independent domination in each parity. Closed neighborhoods have size 22, with intersection size 6 or 0 at center distances 4 or 6. Distance-six pairs form a matching, and an all-distance-four triple has the unique common midpoint given by the intersection of the two weight-four supports after translation. Inclusion–exclusion rules out size at most three and gives coverage 64 for a four-set exactly when its six-edges form a perfect matching. Translating one six-edge to 0,b yields the third and fourth vertices c,b+c. Counting gives 224×10/2=1120 per parity and 1,254,400 labeled unions. Independent exhaustive checks for both parities found the same histogram and zero affine identity failures; replay: python3 /workspace/branches/0eff1380-a90f-4137-a7be-b2d0e5aa6000/independent_replay.py 7. The claim is specifically the seven-cube, not general dimension.
